profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the U.S.-based evaluation lead and the Peru-based partnership coordinator for a new pilot of a collaboration framework intended to assess international university-led water research partnerships across three upcoming partner engagements. The context is that they need to align interfaces between the evaluation workstream and the on-the-ground partnership workstream before materials go to a binational steering committee. The agenda is to confirm which pilot sites are included in the first round, agree on what counts as the baseline being complete, coordinate how interview materials will be handed off, and confirm they are both using the same framework version for the steering committee packet. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on timeline, deliverables, and handoffs for the pilot rollout, without realizing they retain different assumptions about scope, status, versioning, and submission format.

members.name: Dr. Lena Hart
members.expertise: Mixed-methods evaluation, research partnership assessment, cross-institutional framework design
members.background: An associate professor at a U.S. university who led the drafting of the collaboration framework and has worked on multi-country academic partnership evaluations funded by foundations and federal grants.
members.private_state: She wants the steering committee to see the pilot as on schedule and methodologically tidy, and she is especially concerned about maintaining comparability across partner cases so the framework looks scalable beyond the original Arequipa collaboration.
hidden_assumptions: When people discuss a 'site' in this pilot, they mean one institutional partnership case, not a field location or watershed study area.
A baseline is effectively complete once the instrument set, roster, and scheduling plan are locked, because actual interviewing is an execution step rather than a planning dependency.
Interview packets should be uploaded in the standard Teams folder as English-ready analysis inputs, not as raw bilingual field materials.
The framework version everyone is using is the November 6 working document on Box, since that is the version with the final domain numbering she has been tracking internally.

members.name: Carlos Quispe
members.expertise: International research operations, bilingual stakeholder coordination, field logistics for water and agriculture projects
members.background: A Peru-based program manager who supports university-community research collaborations, coordinates interviews and workshops across local institutions, and regularly translates between academic planning language and field implementation realities.
members.private_state: He wants to avoid overpromising to local partners and is focused on making sure the process respects existing relationships, municipal schedules, and bilingual documentation practices, while still appearing responsive to the U.S. team.
hidden_assumptions: When people refer to 'pilot sites,' they usually mean the local project locations or basin-based cases where stakeholders are actually being engaged.
A baseline is not complete until at least the first round of stakeholder interviews has been conducted, because otherwise there is nothing concrete to baseline against.
Uploading interview packets means placing the raw working materials in the shared Google Drive folder used by local coordinators, including Spanish notes, recordings, and transcripts.
The current framework is the November 28 translated PDF that circulated by email, because that is the version local partners reviewed and commented on.
If local utility or community-facing partners are already attending coordination meetings, they are implicitly part of the partner engagement list unless someone explicitly removes them.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as a pilot site
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree to start with 'three pilot sites' in the first round.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means three institutional partnership cases: the Arequipa collaboration plus two additional university-led international partnerships being used as comparable evaluation cases.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means three local implementation locations within the Arequipa collaboration: the Majes irrigation area, the upper Chili watershed, and the urban water quality case around Arequipa.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In water research, 'site' naturally refers to a field location, while in evaluation work it naturally refers to a case unit; because both interpretations sound standard and both involve the number three, the phrase feels fully aligned.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree the 'baseline should be complete by May 15' before the steering committee review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes baseline completion means the framework domains are mapped, stakeholder roster finalized, interview guides approved, and scheduling windows confirmed, making the pilot ready for data collection.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes baseline completion means at least the first round of interviews or surveys has already been conducted at each pilot site so there is actual starting-condition evidence to summarize.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The term 'baseline' routinely refers both to preparatory setup and to collected starting-point data, and both standards are professionally reasonable; because they are discussing status at a high level, neither expects the other to spell out the threshold.

misalignment_points.topic: What goes into the interview packet handoff
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree Carlos will 'drop the interview packets in the shared folder' after each round.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects a standardized packet in the Teams evaluation folder containing the consent tracker, an anonymized transcript or summary in English, and the structured memo aligned to framework domains.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects to upload a practical field packet to the Google Drive operations folder containing audio files, Spanish notes, local scheduling context, and rough transcripts for later processing.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both teams already use shared cloud spaces and both call their handoff bundle a 'packet,' so the phrase sounds operationally settled even though they silently differ on tool, level of processing, and required contents.

misalignment_points.topic: Which November framework version is current
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to using 'the November framework' for the steering committee packet.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the November 6 Box draft with revised domain numbering and notes for evaluators, which she considers the working master.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the November 28 translated PDF emailed to local partners, which includes slightly different labels and examples and is the most recent document he saw used externally.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both documents are legitimately from November and both have been circulated in overlapping channels; saying 'the November framework' feels specific enough in context, so neither notices they are anchored to different files.
